h.strategy: Read the retrieved abstracts for measured results that contradict common heuristics: options that were expected to be weak but did well, gains that vanished in strong configurations, or components whose value depended on what else was present. Turn each such finding into a conditional claim about when a one-field edit's effect is larger or smaller. Each hypothesis must cite the kind of evidence it rests on in one sentence. Avoid hypotheses that only restate that removing an alternative path makes the remaining path matter more. Vary the edited and conditioning fields, and balance HIGHER and LOWER.

hyps.why: Prior benchmark results show skip connections help mainly where trainable depth is missing, so the gain shrinks when the deep path through node 2 already carries a strong 3x3 conv.
Cell-level results show a conv's value depends on whether its output reaches the cell output, and with edge 4 removed node 1 only reaches node 3 through the longer route via node 2.
Node 2 feeds the output only through edge 5, so a conv on edge 1 contributes little when edge 5 is none.
Benchmark ablations show that replacing a removed connection with any parametric op gives much larger gains than swapping between working ops.
Pooling was expected to be a harmless cheap op, but swapping out a 3x3 conv for it costs far more accuracy than swapping out weaker ops.
A conv replacing a missing direct input-to-output edge adds a new path, whereas replacing a skip connection can remove a useful gradient shortcut.
Evidence of diminishing returns from stacking convs shows the 3x3 gain is smaller when node 2 already receives a 3x3-processed input.
Cells with a removed final-stage edge are among the weakest in the benchmark, so adding a 3x3 conv there recovers far more accuracy than replacing an existing op.
Skip connections were expected to be weak but are consistently strong at restoring connectivity, so replacing none with skip gives a large and reliable gain.
Component value depends on what else is present, and a skip on edge 2 is largely redundant when edge 1 already supplies an identity path into node 2.
